title: Covariate-Adjusted Rosenbaum Rank Inversion under Heterogeneous Effects and Outlier Contamination
banked_reason: Stage 0.5 typed verdict: tier=subfield below field floor; paper_score_ceiling 6.5 < 7.4; salvageable=false.
gap_reasons: Its regular inference theorem requires fixed covariate cells and a strong root-N smooth approximation to finite-population pair cdfs, so it does not establish the advertised frontier for ordinary heterogeneous experiments generally.
The contamination boundary is sharp within the constructed one-outlier family; it is not a general robustness boundary, as the note ultimately states.
No application or numerical evaluation shows how often the regularity conditions hold or whether the conservative interval is useful in practice, limiting its projected leading-journal score.
proof_attempt_summary: The run completed the exact pooled estimator's heterogeneous target, joint first-stage/rank influence law, global endpoint inversion, feasible cell-sharp variance envelope, and a quantified one-outlier contamination phase diagram; both mathematical and decision referees passed, and the Li–Ding CLT citation was verified from its primary source. The field-tier bid collapsed because the positive theorem rests on fixed cells and a strong root-N pair-cdf approximation, while robustness sharpness remains family-specific and the paper has no substantive empirical evaluation. A future re-raise must broaden the ordinary-experiment class and likely add a real application rather than restating the finished subfield theorem.
tldr: The exact pooled projection-residual Rosenbaum inversion estimates an allocation-dependent finite-population residual-pair median under heterogeneous effects. On a common fixed-cell square-tail envelope, its global endpoints admit a joint pooled-OLS/rank Gaussian law that retains first-stage estimation; attainable cell-conditional variance bounds have uniformly consistent observed-data endpoints and yield conservative coverage. A bounded-covariate one-outlier family makes the regularity boundary rate-sharp: contamination below \(\sqrt N\) is negligible, at \(\sqrt N\) it adds an unestimable Gaussian-plus-Bernoulli variance component, between \(\sqrt N\) and \(N\) it slows consistency, and at order \(N\) it produces assignment-conditional inconsistency and a \(7/10\) shrinking-interval coverage ceiling for a two-array comparison.
gap: The published adjusted theorem assumes a constant additive effect; its heterogeneous Section 5 result is unadjusted. Existing generated-statistic and sharp-bound results do not identify the source’s pooled heterogeneous rank law. Lei (2024) identifies a different rank-OLS coefficient under random assignment, leaving the pooled-residual inversion question untouched.
fill: Prove a source-faithful joint inversion law and usable cell-sharp bound under a transparent finite-support regularity class, then delimit an explicit contamination boundary.
